# Python Environments {background-color="#288DC2"}

## 

![](../figures/xkcd_python-env.png){fig-align="center"}

## Managing your Python environment

A Python environment is composed of the **Python version** and **library versions** (including dependencies)

```{python}
#| code-line-numbers: "|1-3|1,3,5-7,14-18|2,9-12"

import polars as pl
from plotnine import *
from pyprojroot.here import here

# Load data.
customer_data = pl.read_csv(here('data/customer_data.csv'))
store_transactions = pl.read_csv(here('data/store_transactions.csv'))

# Visualize customers by region.
(ggplot(customer_data, aes(x = 'region'))
  + geom_bar()
)

# Number of customers by region.
(customer_data
  .group_by(pl.col('region'))
  .agg(n = pl.len())
)
```

## Managing your Python environment

A Python environment is composed of the **Python version** and **library versions** (including dependencies) and it is not uncommon for different projects to require **different Python versions** and **different library versions**

::: {.incremental}
- A **virtual environment** (a.k.a., a **project environment**) is a self-contained, project-specific environment
- Project environments can be **reproduced on another machine** by you (including future you) or someone else
- If you need to reproduce something about your machine beyond your code, Python version, and library versions, you'll want to use a **container**
:::

::: {.fragment}
This is part of the reason why in some courses you'll use a **cloud-based solution** (e.g., Google Colab) where the Python environment is managed for you
:::

# Miscellaneous {background-color="#288DC2"}

## Concluding thoughts

Code is transparent and reproducible, but Python is a *big tent* so follow your professor's or mentor's instructions

::: {.incremental}
- Data analysis vs. software development
- Code is interactive---leverage it to confirm what you're learning
- AI can accelerate productivity, but it can't replace learning
- You have human help---professors, peers, TAs, the ASC, etc.
:::

## {background-color="#0F2439"}

### Application {.lato-font}

1. Install uv (visit [docs.astral.sh/uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)) via the command line
2. Restart the command line and install Python using `uv python install` via the command line
3. Register for a GitHub account with a *professional username* using your student email address (visit [github.com](https://github.com)) and download this workshop repository (visit [github.com/marcdotson/pydata-python](https://github.com/marcdotson/pydata-python))
4. Download and install VS Code (visit [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com)) and the Python extension in VS Code
5. Inside VS Code, open the downloaded workshop repository and activate the project environment with `uv run` via the terminal
6. Use and modify the Python script or notebook and explore the included data
